title: Compact neighbourhood bases in weakly locally compact Hausdorff spaces
statement: Let $T$ be a Hausdorff topological space, meaning that distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods. Suppose every $t\in T$ has a compact neighbourhood. Here $N\subseteq T$ is a neighbourhood of $t$ if it contains an open set containing $t$, and subsets carry the subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. A subset is compact if every covering by relatively open sets has a finite subcover. Then for every $t\in T$ and every neighbourhood $N$ of $t$, there is a compact neighbourhood $K$ of $t$ with $K\subseteq N$.
